comments.body:
Pushed as Gerrit change 2671 (commit 866e6dd6d46c). Recording the decisions and the evidence
behind them so they live on the ticket rather than only in the commit.

## The mechanism question, answered with evidence rather than by picking the easy one

The ticket offered a runtime storage quota "when compatible with current overlay2/root
filesystem", else a bounded reaper. The quota is NOT compatible on this host and the daemon
says so in one line: overlay2's `--storage-opt size=` (and the `overlay2.size` daemon default)
is refused unless the filesystem backing /var/lib/docker is XFS mounted with `pquota` --
`--storage-opt is supported only for overlay over xfs with 'pquota' mount option`. That
filesystem is ROOT here, XFS reads quota options at MOUNT time and refuses them on a remount,
so enabling it needs `rootflags=pquota` on the kernel command line and a REBOOT. That is the
same constraint S4 (`2ba3-bf77`) hit for /var/tmp, re-derived for this mechanism, and it binds
here too. Two further limits even after that reboot: the quota is PER-CONTAINER rather than an
aggregate ceiling over the share, and it applies at container CREATION, so every live service
would have to be recreated to acquire one.

`container_quota_enforceable` publishes which regime the box is in, unalarmed for S4's reason:
its honest value is 0 until that reboot is scheduled, and an alarm that pages continuously is
muted within a day. `container_reaper_active` IS alarmed -- that pre-empts the finding S4's
plan review raised, since a byte cap enforced by a timer with no liveness signal can stop
existing silently while every other reading stays nominal.

## What it does NOT guarantee, with the number

Stated first because it is sharper than S4's fill rate: THE REAPER CANNOT RECLAIM A RUNNING
CONTAINER'S WRITABLE LAYER AT ALL. Only exited/dead containers are removable, so for the live
compose set this story delivers measurement and an alarm, NOT a bound. For the debris it does
reach, the bound between two runs is `cap + fill_rate x interval`: at the 2 GiB share and a
300 s period a sustained net fill above ~7.2 MB/s exceeds the share before the reaper next
runs, and this gp3 volume does 125 MB/s baseline -- roughly 17x. A single runaway writer
defeats it; its real job is bounding steady debris accumulation.

## Why it is NOT `docker container prune`, and how the live set was proved spared

The ticket names `docker container prune --filter until=...`. Its filter set is `until` and
`label` only, with NO name filter, and that is not sufficient here. `autodeploy.sh` starts the
mcp blue-green backends with a BARE `docker run` that compose never sees (`mcp_run_new`), and
reaps them itself in `mcp_retire_sweep` under a guard this reaper cannot replicate: it reads
the nginx `/mcp/` upstream include and REFUSES to reap an exited container that is still the
live backend, because `--restart always` would otherwise have restored it. Reaping one anyway
is bug `9ea3-7d07`: a transient exit became a PERMANENT 502 on 2026-09-02.

So candidates are enumerated and removed one at a time, sparing three overlapping sets --
anything `com.docker.compose.project`-labelled, anything carrying `mcp_run_new`'s
`rebar.service` identity label, and anything matching `^(rebar-mcp|compose-mcp-1)`. A test
asserts that last pattern is byte-identical to `mcp_managed`'s own regex in autodeploy.sh, so
the two cannot drift. Two further guarantees come from the DAEMON rather than this shell:
candidates come from `docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=dead`, which never
lists a running container, and removal is `docker rm` WITHOUT `-f`, which the daemon refuses
for a running container -- the property `mcp_retire_image` already relies on for images. No
`-v`/`--volumes` is ever passed and `docker system prune` is never used.

## One budget, not a second cap

ADR 0112 and docker-storage-cap.sh's own header both anticipated this story: writable layers
live INSIDE /var/lib/docker, so two caps over the same bytes are either double-counted or
mutually violable. `DOCKER_CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES` (2 GiB) is therefore carved OUT of the
existing 20 GiB budget -- BuildKit 5 + writable 2 + images 13 = 20 GiB, images having been 15
-- and container-cap.sh READS it rather than re-spelling it. When it cannot read it, it reaps
NOTHING and says so: a reaper running against a guessed ceiling would delete containers to
satisfy a number nobody chose (autodeploy's `prune_docker_caches` takes the same position on
the BuildKit cap).

The 2 GiB is labelled as an ADR 0112 decision-6 starting point rather than a measurement: no
writable-layer figure was captured at the 2026-09-02 outage, since `docker system df`'s
Containers row was never recorded.

## Verification

14/14 seeded defects were caught by a NAMED test, including the three protected sets, the
grace window, `-f`, the low-water mark, the guessed-share fallback, accounting-vs-enforcement,
publish-a-0-instead-of-silence, a heartbeat gated on the docker read, notBreaching, a dropped
alarm, the budget arithmetic, and an alarm on the quota reading. Two seeded defects initially
escaped and both exposed genuinely weak tests, which were tightened rather than accepted: the
low-water-mark test now uses sizes at which "reap to the ceiling" and "reap to 80%" disagree,
and the under-share test now uses 90% of the share -- the region between the stop target and
the trigger, where a token-sized container proved nothing.

Terraform was written and VALIDATED (`fmt -check` clean, `validate` Success) and never applied.
lint, typecheck, and the complexity and mechanism ratchets are clean (new=0 increased=0). 675
tests pass across the new suites plus every existing suite that drives observability.sh,
docker-storage-cap.sh or compose-up.sh.

## Known limitation, consistent with the siblings

A change to container-cap.sh alone does not re-run its installer: `compose-up.sh` is in
autodeploy's MATERIALIZER_PATHS but the cap scripts are not, exactly as for docker-storage-cap,
journald-cap and vartmp-cap. The reaper unit runs from the installed copy under
/usr/local/bin, so an edit reaches the box on the next compose-up. A stale unit is DETECTED
rather than silent -- that is what `container_reaper_active` and
`rebar-container-reaper-not-active` are for. Left consistent with the siblings rather than
changed unilaterally here.

compiled_state.description:
## Why
Writable container layers are each container's overlay2 `upperdir`. They grow independently of
image layers and build cache, no prune reaches them, and nothing measured them on 2026-09-02 —
the only signal was "root disk high". The last cap under ADR 0112.

## Mechanism decision, with evidence
The ticket offers a runtime storage quota "when compatible", else a reaper. **The quota is NOT
compatible here.** overlay2's `--storage-opt size=` (and the `overlay2.size` daemon default) is
accepted only when the filesystem backing `/var/lib/docker` is XFS mounted with `pquota`, else
the daemon refuses: `--storage-opt is supported only for overlay over xfs with 'pquota' mount
option`. That filesystem is ROOT here, and XFS reads quota options at MOUNT time and refuses
them on a remount — so it needs `rootflags=pquota` and a REBOOT: the constraint S4 (`2ba3`) hit
for `/var/tmp`. Even then it is PER-CONTAINER, not an aggregate ceiling, and applies at
creation, so every live service must be recreated. So this ships the mitigation and publishes which
regime the box is in; the runbook carries the enablement steps.

## What the reaper does NOT guarantee
1. **It cannot reclaim a RUNNING container's writable layer at all.** Only exited/dead ones are
   removable, so for the live compose set this is MEASUREMENT AND AN ALARM, not a bound; only
   the reboot-gated quota would bound those.
2. For the debris it does bound, the bound is `cap + fill_rate x interval`: at 2 GiB and 300 s a
   sustained net fill above ~7.2 MB/s outruns it, and this gp3 volume does 125 MB/s (~17x).
3. Nothing that exited inside the 900 s grace window is removed; when it cannot get under the
   share it SAYS SO.

## Safety — proved against the live set
`docker container prune --filter until=…` cannot express what this host needs: its filters are
`until` and `label` only, with no name filter. `autodeploy.sh` starts the mcp blue-green backends
with a bare `docker run` compose never sees and reaps them in `mcp_retire_sweep` under a guard
this reaper cannot replicate: it reads the nginx `/mcp/` upstream include and refuses to reap an
exited container still named as the live backend, since `--restart always` would have restored
it — bug `9ea3`, a transient exit that became a permanent 502 on 2026-09-02. So candidates are
removed one by one, sparing:

* `com.docker.compose.project`-labelled (gerrit, review-bot, opcert, compose-mcp-1): an exited
  compose service is a crashed one whose logs are the evidence;
* `rebar.service`-labelled;
* matching `^(rebar-mcp|compose-mcp-1)` — `mcp_managed`'s regex, so the two agree.

Two guarantees the DAEMON enforces, not shell logic: candidates come from `docker ps -a --filter
status=exited --filter status=dead`, which never lists a running container, and removal is
`docker rm` WITHOUT `-f`, which the daemon refuses for a running one. No `-v`/`--volumes`, and
never `docker system prune`.

**Three thresholds, stated once.** Reaping TRIGGERS only when the footprint exceeds 100% of the
share; it STOPS at the 80% low-water mark, so a set at the boundary is not evicted every tick;
the ALARM fires at 85%. A footprint at 90% therefore reaps NOTHING while the alarm has fired.

**Sizes.** ONE `docker inspect --size` gives the total and each candidate's `SizeRw` — the field
`docker system df` sums into its Containers row, so census and ledger cannot disagree. The loop
sorts by `State.FinishedAt` ASCENDING and SUBTRACTS each removed size from its running total; it
never re-reads the ledger per removal, which could not converge under concurrent writes.

## What invokes the reaper, and what publishes its heartbeat
Two DIFFERENT callers. The REAPER runs
from its own `rebar-container-reaper.timer` (5 min; `TimeoutStartSec` nests below the period,
bug `1205`), rendered by `--print-units` and installed by `compose-up.sh` beside the three
caps it already installs — a timer rather than an autodeploy hook, since `prune_docker_caches`
runs only on deploy/backoff/pressure paths. The HEARTBEAT comes from
`observability.sh`'s existing 5-minute timer, whose §2i calls the side-effect-free
`--check-active` — so "every tick" is the OBSERVABILITY tick, and the heartbeat still has a
producer when the reaper timer is the dead thing.

## Observability (publish-or-stay-silent)
§2i, from the SAME single `docker system df` call §2f already makes — its format string gains
`{{.Reclaimable}}`, not a second daemon walk.
Three DF-DERIVED readings: `container_writable_bytes`, `container_exited_bytes` and
`container_writable_used_percent` (`pct_of_cap`, reused). Plus two 1/0 ALWAYS-PUBLISH STATE METRICS, `container_reaper_active` (the heartbeat) and
`container_quota_enforceable`, whose PROBES are: `systemctl is-active` on the timer AND the
installed unit matching what `--print-units` renders; and `xfs_quota -x -c 'state -p'` reporting
`Enforcement: ON`. Both publish on EVERY tick including their 0 path; the df-derived three only
on a parseable Containers row.

## Alarms
`rebar-container-writable-usage-high` (>85%) and `rebar-container-reaper-not-active` (<1), both
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and SNS-wired. **The second pre-empts the S4 finding**:
without it a silently-dead timer leaves usage nominal while nothing enforces anything.
`container_quota_enforceable` gets NO alarm — it reads 0 until the reboot, and a permanently
firing alarm is muted within a day.

## Scope
`docker-storage-cap.sh` owns the BUDGET, `container-cap.sh` only the reaper/checks/rendering.
ADR 0112 puts this share INSIDE the Docker budget, so the former gains
`DOCKER_CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES` (2 GiB, a decision-6 starting point) carved out of the
existing 20 GiB — BuildKit 5 + this 2 + images 13 = 20 —
and `container-cap.sh` READS it, so no second literal drifts.

In: NEW `infra/scripts/container-cap.sh`; `docker-storage-cap.sh` (third share);
`observability.sh` (§2i + extended parse); `compose-up.sh` (installs the timer);
`monitoring_autodeploy.tf`; `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`;
`tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py` (its `DOCKER_IMAGE_SHARE_BYTES` assertions move to
the three-way split); `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`; two NEW test files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--reap` removes an exited unowned container when the footprint is OVER the share, and
      nothing when it is under (tested at 90%, between the stop target and the trigger); it
      reaps oldest-exit-first down to 80%, and WARNs naming the running/protected bytes when it
      cannot get under.
- [ ] `--reap` removes nothing for each of: a `running` row; a `com.docker.compose.project` or
      `rebar.service` label; a `rebar-mcp-*` / `compose-mcp-1` name; an exit inside the grace
      window; an unreadable share. Its argv never contains `-f`, `-v`, `--volumes`,
      `system prune` or `container prune`; a test pins the name pattern to `mcp_managed`'s.
- [ ] `observability.sh` publishes the df-derived readings from a parseable Containers row and
      NONE when absent or unparseable; percent clamped to 100; the state metrics publish every
      tick including their 0 path; all five dimensionless.
- [ ] `--check-active` prints 1 only when the timer is active AND its installed unit matches the
      rendered one — 0 for a dead timer, a stale unit and absent units; `--check-quota` prints 1
      only for `Enforcement: ON`, and 0 for accounting-only, unreadable and no `xfs_quota`.
- [ ] `docker-storage-cap.sh --print-env` states the third share, the three sum to the budget
      (5+2+13=20 GiB), and an over-subscribed split is refused.
- [ ] Both alarms exist by name, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and SNS-wired, nothing
      alarms on `container_quota_enforceable`, and `terraform fmt -check`/`validate` pass.
- [ ] The runbook documents diagnosis, remediation, the `rootflags=pquota` + reboot steps, and
      forbids manual overlay2 deletion.
- [ ] Portability: Docker APIs, systemd, local pytest; no CI-provider trigger.

file_impact.reason: NEW: the writable-layer reaper, the two activation/quota checks, and the reaper unit rendering.
Carve DOCKER_CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES out of the existing Docker budget (one budget, three shares).
Publish writable/exited-container layer usage, cap percent, and the two heartbeats (section 2i).
Install the rebar-container-reaper timer beside the three existing caps.
Writable-layer saturation and reaper-not-active CloudWatch alarms.
Diagnosis, safe remediation, the pquota enablement steps, and no manual overlay2 deletion.
NEW: reaper safety, every protected set, the checks, and the side-effect-free contract.
NEW: metric emission, silence on unmeasurable readings, and both heartbeats.
The split assertions move to the three-way budget.
Assert the two new alarms by name, their SNS wiring, and that the quota reading is NOT alarmed.
